# libreac / fuzz_boxreg

libreac's own fuzz target `fuzz_boxreg` ([source](source/fuzz_boxreg.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over libreac 1.9.0 (FreeREAC/libreac at d16f3f4e).

Runs up to 64 operations of the multi-box registry, reac_boxreg, from the payload: a fabric size, then declare, add, find and set_name calls with input-chosen widths, bases, MACs and names (each name its own allocation), on a registry in its own allocation. Before each call it works out the answer the header promises from the table as it was, and after every call it checks the whole registry.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static libreac.a of every src/*.c of libreac 1.9.0 at commit d16f3f4e, compiled with each build's flags, as libreac's Makefile builds its fuzz targets but with this toolchain in place of a native clang and libFuzzer.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- At most REAC_BOXREG_MAX_BOXES boxes, each of an even width of 2 to 40 (a rule the harness writes out itself) with its slice inside the fabric and a NUL-terminated name; no two slices overlap and no MAC is registered twice ([lines 115-159](source/fuzz_boxreg.c#L115-L159)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- No call moves a box, changes its width or its pinned flag, unbinds or rebinds its MAC, or changes any name but the one set_name sets ([lines 161-185](source/fuzz_boxreg.c#L161-L185)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A declaration is refused for a bad width, a full table or no free range, and otherwise lands at the next index with the width asked for, at the pinned base or the lowest free range, pinned exactly when a base was given, unbound, with the name given; a refused one adds no box ([lines 218-283](source/fuzz_boxreg.c#L218-L283)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- add refuses a bad width or the all-zero MAC, and otherwise gives the MAC's own box, then the first unbound box of that width, then a new unpinned box at the lowest free range; it is idempotent and find finds what it registered ([lines 291-360](source/fuzz_boxreg.c#L291-L360)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- find answers -1 or the index of a box holding exactly that MAC, and never finds the all-zero MAC ([lines 366-382](source/fuzz_boxreg.c#L366-L382)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- set_name stores the name given, or the empty name for NULL, at a valid index ([lines 388-396](source/fuzz_boxreg.c#L388-L396)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

|---|---|---|
| `plain_halts` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2 | [proved](proofs/plain_halts/) |
| `ubsan_halts` | on every input on which the UBSan build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2 | [proved](proofs/ubsan_halts/) |

| `asan_ubsan_halts` | on every input on which the ASan+UBSan build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2 | [proved](proofs/asan_ubsan_halts/) |
| `asan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 2 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; ASan never fires; memory refused only when forced | [proved](proofs/asan_agrees/) |
| `ubsan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; UBSan never fires; memory refused only when forced | [proved](proofs/ubsan_agrees/) |
| `asan_ubsan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 2 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; ASan+UBSan never fires; memory refused only when forced | [proved](proofs/asan_ubsan_agrees/) |

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libreac` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_boxreg.plain` | 47,672 | `76a5b76842fcfa903088d14284b1d3d84d3fa4358e865ab144f74123af312e0c` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_boxreg.ubsan` | 48,696 | `d63ba804708e835e57646043730f6bdd8fc3e34ba6e2204407d533a65213a34d` |
| asan | `fuzz_boxreg.asan` | 569,032 | `eacfa20547ad7dc0d24164010513fcc8af4ba5e557ff3f391a07559e3e34a6df` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzz_boxreg.asan-ubsan` | 570,088 | `7620eb05e0adf5cb5ea350a6fe814d02d6ddb2685ec03477d0d4a85d249b0d85` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
